scope: Supplemental safe classroom experiment concepts only.

experiments.title: Bicarbonate fizz concept
experiments.focus: Observe a safe acid-carbonate gas release conceptually.
student_observations: Bubbles appear when the acid and bicarbonate meet.
Gas formation is a visible sign of change.
experiments.teacher_note: Concept only; the app shows the reaction at a classroom level.

experiments.title: Sugar dissolving
experiments.focus: Show how a soluble solid can disappear into a clear solution.
experiments.teacher_note: Connect the observation to solution particles.

experiments.title: Limestone and acid concept
experiments.focus: Link carbonate materials to gas evolution in a safe concept model.
student_observations: The solid slowly reacts in the model.
experiments.teacher_note: Use as a discussion example, not a real lab recipe.

experiments.title: Solution limit idea
experiments.focus: Introduce the idea that a solution can only dissolve so much solute at a given condition.
student_observations: Extra solid may remain at the bottom.
Warm water can change the limit in the model.
experiments.teacher_note: Describe it conceptually and avoid over-precision.

experiments.title: Magnesium sulfate dissolving
experiments.focus: Show a soluble salt forming a clear solution.
student_observations: The solid dissolves into the liquid.
experiments.teacher_note: Use this as a second soluble-salt example after table salt.

experiments.title: Glucose and sucrose comparison
experiments.focus: Compare two common sugars in the classroom model.
student_observations: The names and formulas are different.
Small changes in formula change the molecule.
experiments.teacher_note: Keep the discussion focused on molecules and formulas, not diet or health.

sources.supports: Melting, boiling, evaporation and condensation concepts.
